items.en: Cameroon separatist leader pleads not guilty at war crimes trial in Norway
items.zh: 喀麥隆分離派領袖在挪威戰爭罪審判中否認指控
items.summary: Lucas Cho Ayaba, a leader of Cameroon's anglophone separatist movement, pleaded not guilty as his war crimes trial opened in Norway. Prosecutors accuse him of remotely directing attacks from Norwegian soil that killed and injured dozens of civilians in Cameroon's North-West and South-West regions. The case is one of the first to test a European court's reach over a diaspora figure accused of commanding violence abroad, and its outcome could shape how states prosecute remote incitement. Al Jazeera notes the trial draws attention to a conflict that has displaced hundreds of thousands since 2017.

items.en: US sanctions on Lebanon's Hezbollah-affiliates may have limited impact
items.zh: 分析指美國對真主黨關聯方的制裁效果有限
items.summary: Analysts told Al Jazeera that fresh US sanctions targeting individuals and firms affiliated with Hezbollah are unlikely to meaningfully weaken the group, which operates largely outside Lebanon's formal banking system. The measures may instead squeeze ordinary Lebanese by further deterring foreign banks from dealing with the country, deepening a financial crisis already in its seventh year. Lebanon's economy remains heavily cash-based, limiting the reach of designations aimed at financial networks. The report frames the sanctions as political signalling toward Washington's domestic audience as much as an instrument of pressure on the group itself.

items.en: Qatar urges restraint and dialogue amid US-Iran tensions
items.zh: 卡達呼籲美伊雙方克制並回到對話
items.summary: Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman called on the United States and Iran to show restraint and return to dialogue as tensions between the two rise. Doha, which has repeatedly acted as an intermediary between Washington and Tehran, warned that escalation would destabilise the Gulf and endanger shipping and energy flows through the region. The appeal comes amid renewed sanctions activity and warnings over the Strait of Hormuz. Al Jazeera reports Qatar is pressing for de-escalation through quiet diplomacy rather than public ultimatums, consistent with its role in earlier rounds of indirect talks.

items.en: China probes Shanghai party chief Chen Jining over corruption
items.zh: 中國以貪腐調查上海市委書記陳吉寧
items.summary: China has opened a corruption investigation into Chen Jining, the Communist Party secretary of Shanghai, making him the fourth Politburo member placed under investigation since last year. The move extends President Xi Jinping's long-running anti-corruption campaign into the party's upper ranks and into its most economically important city. Chen, a former environmental scientist and Beijing mayor, had been seen as a technocratic riser. Al Jazeera reports that the pattern of senior-level probes signals continued consolidation of political control ahead of leadership reshuffles, rather than a narrowly financial enforcement drive.

items.en: Five women killed every hour globally by partner, relative last year: UN
items.zh: 聯合國：去年全球每小時有五名女性遭伴侶或親屬殺害
items.summary: UN Women reported that roughly five women and girls were killed every hour worldwide last year by an intimate partner or family member, meaning the home remains the most dangerous place for them. The agency said the figure has barely shifted in years despite national action plans and awareness campaigns, pointing to weak enforcement, under-reporting and inconsistent data collection. Africa recorded the highest rate relative to population. The report, released around the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, calls for funded prevention services rather than legislation alone.

items.en: Nvidia stock cools after Huang's return-driven surge
items.zh: 輝達股價在黃仁勳回任行情後明顯降溫
items.summary: Nvidia shares fell back after the rally triggered by Jensen Huang's reinstatement as chief executive, which had restored about $952bn in market value in a single session. Huang returned less than two weeks after resigning, and investors initially treated the reversal as removing a major governance risk. The pullback suggests scepticism about whether leadership alone resolves questions over AI capital spending and customer concentration. Al Jazeera reports the swing underlines how dependent the wider market has become on a single company's news flow, with chip peers moving in step with Nvidia.

items.en: US tightens AI chip export controls, adds Alibaba unit to trade blacklist
items.zh: 美國收緊 AI 晶片出口管制，阿里巴巴子公司列入貿易黑名單
items.summary: Washington tightened export controls on advanced AI chips and added an Alibaba subsidiary to its trade blacklist, according to Taiwan's Central News Agency. The listing restricts the entity from receiving US-origin technology without a licence, and officials said the step targets channels used to route restricted accelerators into China. Separately, the firm Megaspeed was designated over alleged help in obtaining Nvidia AI chips. The move extends a multi-year effort to limit Chinese access to frontier compute, and raises compliance pressure on Taiwanese suppliers that sit in the middle of those supply chains.

items.en: MediaTek deepens edge-to-cloud AI research with 17 journal papers this year
items.zh: 聯發科深耕邊緣到雲端 AI，今年 17 篇論文入選國際期刊
items.summary: MediaTek said it had 17 papers accepted by international journals and conferences this year, covering work that spans on-device inference through to cloud AI infrastructure, Taiwan's Central News Agency reported. The company framed the output as evidence that its research pipeline now reaches beyond smartphone silicon into data-centre adjacent design. Taiwan also placed 10 papers in the 2027 International Solid-State Circuits Conference. For students and engineers, the figures are a useful signal of which research directions Taiwanese chip firms are staffing up, particularly edge AI and heterogeneous computing.

items.en: How Senegal got their AFCON trophy back
items.zh: 塞內加爾如何討回非洲盃冠軍獎盃
items.summary: Al Jazeera examined how Senegal's disputed Africa Cup of Nations title ended up before sport's highest court and was ultimately restored to them. The case turned on an administrative ruling rather than on-field play, and it exposed gaps in how the continental federation handles eligibility and protest procedures. Senegalese officials argued the original decision punished the squad for a paperwork failing outside the players' control. The resolution hands the trophy back but leaves questions about appeal timelines and the precedent set for future tournaments, which rivals are already citing in their own filings.

items.en: African rivals fret over Morocco's growing football dominance
items.zh: 摩洛哥足球聲勢壯大，非洲對手憂心不平
items.summary: Morocco's run of success on the pitch and its expanding influence in continental football administration has prompted complaints from rivals that it benefits from preferential treatment. Supporters counter that sustained investment in academies, infrastructure and a professional domestic league simply set an example others have not matched. The country is also central to upcoming hosting plans, giving it scheduling and commercial advantages. Al Jazeera weighs both readings, noting that the debate is less about any single refereeing decision than about how resources and governance power have concentrated in one federation.

items.en: Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund: UEFA Champions League
items.zh: 歐冠：兵工廠主場對決多特蒙德
items.summary: Al Jazeera ran live coverage of Arsenal's Champions League meeting with Borussia Dortmund, with Martin Odegaard headlining the team news. The fixture carried weight for both sides' qualification maths in the league phase, where a single result can swing seeding for the knockout rounds. Arsenal came in needing to protect a strong home record, while Dortmund travelled with questions over defensive consistency. The build-up focused on midfield control and whether Dortmund's press could disrupt Arsenal's build-up play, a matchup that has decided several of their recent European meetings.

items.en: School environment plays key role in shaping parents' educational hopes for their children
items.zh: 研究：校園環境明顯影響家長對子女的教育期望
items.summary: A study reported by Phys.org finds that the school environment a child attends substantially shapes how ambitious their parents' educational expectations are, independent of family income or parental schooling. Researchers found that peer composition, teacher expectations and visible pathways to higher education all raised the level of attainment parents considered realistic. The finding matters because parental expectation is itself one of the stronger predictors of a student's eventual attainment, suggesting school placement effects compound over time. The authors argue interventions aimed only at families may miss a key institutional driver of aspiration.

items.en: Global higher education enrolments 'to peak by 2036'
items.zh: 全球高等教育入學人數預估 2036 年前見頂
items.summary: Times Higher Education reports projections that worldwide higher education enrolment will peak by 2036 before declining, driven primarily by falling birth rates across East Asia, Europe and increasingly Latin America. Analysts warn that institutions planning capacity on decades of assumed growth face structural over-supply, with mid-ranked regional universities most exposed. Growth is expected to continue only in parts of Africa and South Asia. The forecast has implications for recruitment strategy, international student dependence and funding models, and suggests competition for domestic students in mature systems will intensify well before the peak arrives.

items.en: 'Unfinished Beginnings': Art installation for children affected by war
items.zh: 「未完成的開始」：為戰火中兒童而作的裝置藝術
items.summary: Artist Bachir Mohamad's installation 'Unfinished Beginnings' uses 20,000 baby bottles to represent children whose early lives have been interrupted by armed conflict. The piece is built to be walked through, so the scale registers physically rather than statistically, a choice the artist describes as resisting the numbing effect of casualty figures. Al Jazeera's coverage situates the work within a wider body of art addressing the developmental and psychological costs borne by children in war zones, where disrupted schooling and chronic stress exposure produce effects that outlast the fighting itself.

items.en: Anthropic stock sinks below $83 IPO price
items.zh: Anthropic 股價跌破 83 美元 IPO 發行價
items.summary: Anthropic shares fell below their $83 initial public offering price, CNBC reported, a reversal for one of the year's most closely watched listings. The slide came as AI-linked names broadly retreated and investors reassessed how quickly frontier model developers can convert revenue growth into durable margins given enormous compute costs. Buyers who entered at the opening trade are now holding sizeable losses. The move is being read as a test of whether public markets will fund the next phase of model training spending, and it pressures peers still weighing listings of their own.

items.en: Huang's return reshapes outlook for Taiwan's AI supply chain
items.zh: 黃仁勳重掌輝達，台廠 AI 供應鏈影響一次看
items.summary: Central News Agency surveyed how Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia chief executive changes the outlook for Taiwanese suppliers, from TSMC's advanced packaging through server ODMs, thermal module makers and high-speed PCB vendors. Executives quoted said the immediate worry about strategy discontinuity has eased, which matters because Taiwanese capacity decisions are made against Nvidia's roadmap years in advance. Cathay's Lee Chang-keng said supply chain anxiety is temporarily resolved. The report cautions that order visibility, not leadership, remains the variable that will decide 2027 capital spending across the island's chain.

items.en: Chip stocks cool as AI outlook clouds; Nvidia falls nearly 6%
items.zh: AI 熱潮前景不明，美股收跌、輝達挫近 6%
items.summary: US equities mostly closed lower as semiconductor shares gave back part of the previous session's surge, with Nvidia down almost 6%, Central News Agency reported. Micron and AMD fell harder still, and the pullback broadened into memory and analogue names. The decline followed a record-setting rally and reflected renewed doubts about the pace of AI capital expenditure rather than any single disclosure. The Dow bucked the trend, closing above 50,000 for the first time as money rotated toward industrials and defensives, a split that points to narrowing conviction in the AI trade.

items.en: Kenshi Yonezu to play Taipei Dome in December, a first for a Japanese solo act
items.zh: 米津玄師 12 月唱進台北大巨蛋，日本歌手第一人
items.summary: Kenshi Yonezu will perform two nights at the Taipei Dome in December, making him the first Japanese solo artist to headline the venue, Taiwanese media reported. The shows form part of his largest world tour to date, covering 11 cities and 14 dates with roughly 200,000 tickets expected. Taipei Dome's capacity places the booking well above his previous Taiwan arena shows, and the dates reportedly overlap with another major Japanese act's Taipei run. Fans should watch the official tour channels for the registration window and ticketing platform details.

items.en: King Gnu confirms Bangkok, Hong Kong, Taipei and Seoul dates for CEN+RAL Tour 2026
items.zh: King Gnu 公布 CEN+RAL Tour 2026 曼谷、香港、台北、首爾場次細節
items.summary: Sony Music Japan published full details for the Asian leg of King Gnu's CEN+RAL Tour 2026, naming Bangkok, Hong Kong, Taipei and Seoul. The announcement is part of what the label describes as the band's largest Asian tour, beginning February 2026. For Taiwan-based fans the Taipei date is the key entry, with venue, on-sale timing and fan club priority windows set out on the official page. Asian legs for Japanese rock acts typically sell through local promoters rather than Japanese ticketing, so checking the Taiwanese partner's site is worthwhile.

items.en: Official HIGE DANDISM announces Asia Tour 2026 including Taipei
items.zh: Official髭男dism 公布 2026 亞洲巡演，台北在列
items.summary: Official HIGE DANDISM will stage an Asia tour from August 2026 covering four cities, with Seoul, Taipei, Singapore and Bangkok reported across six shows. It is the band's first Asian run in about two years. The scheduling puts the Taipei date in the summer window, which usually means ticket registration opens several months ahead through a Taiwanese promoter. Given how quickly their previous Taipei show sold, fans planning to attend should register for the official fan club in advance, since priority ballots typically close before general sale opens.

items.en: YOASOBI announces 10-city Asia tour spanning 2026 and 2027
items.zh: YOASOBI 公布橫跨 2026 至 2027 的十城亞洲巡演
items.summary: YOASOBI announced a 10-city Asia tour running across 2026 and 2027, their largest regional itinerary so far. Coverage of the announcement lists stops across East and Southeast Asia, with individual venue and on-sale details rolled out market by market rather than all at once. For Taiwan and Hong Kong fans that means watching the duo's official accounts for the local promoter announcement. The scale of the routing reflects how much of the duo's streaming audience now sits outside Japan, following anime tie-ins that travelled well across the region.
